title: Amazon’s Most Beloved Features May Turn Out to Be Illegal

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店当DJ的黑胶唱片时代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去上班，把DJ台变成一个充满50年历史精美文物的流动快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Last week, when the U.S.
sentences.zh: 上周，当美国

sentences.en: government filed a landmark antitrust lawsuit against Amazon, it pointed to a set of familiar features that have made Amazon so beloved by consumers.
sentences.zh: 政府对亚马逊提起了一项具有里程碑意义的反垄断诉讼时，它指出了亚马逊深受消费者喜爱的一系列熟悉功能。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Karen Weiss on why those beloved features may actually be illegal.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事凯伦·韦斯将为您解析这些深受喜爱功能为何可能实际上是违法的。

sentences.en: It's Monday, October 2nd.
sentences.zh: 今天是10月2日，星期一。

sentences.en: Karen, now that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 凯伦，既然美国

sentences.en: government has actually sued Amazon for monopolistic tactics, we wanted to talk to you, somebody who has covered Amazon for years,
sentences.zh: 政府已经正式起诉亚马逊采取垄断策略，我们想和你这位报道亚马逊多年的记者聊聊，

sentences.en: about the very specific ways that Amazon has allegedly broken the law.
sentences.zh: 关于亚马逊涉嫌违法的一些具体手段。

sentences.en: So, talk us through that.
sentences.zh: 那么，请给我们详细讲讲。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, the Federal Trade Commission looked at a lot of things, but they said in the end it kind of boiled down to two tactics that are behind the scenes of things that we all know.
sentences.zh: 联邦贸易委员会调查了很多方面，但他们表示，最终归结为两种策略，而这两种策略正是我们所熟知事物背后的推手。

sentences.en: So, one is how we buy things on Amazon.
sentences.zh: 首先是我们如何在亚马逊上购物。

sentences.en: When you click buy, the buy now button, and then also prime shipping, that's super fast shipping that is part of how things get to your door so quickly.
sentences.zh: 当你点击“立即购买”按钮，还有Prime配送，那种能让商品如此迅速送到你门口的超快配送服务。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: What you just mentioned are basically the throbbing heart of my relationship with Amazon.
sentences.zh: 你刚才提到的基本上就是我和亚马逊关系的命脉所在。

sentences.en: I assume everyone's relationship to Amazon.
sentences.zh: 我想这也是每个人与亚马逊的关系。

sentences.en: And you're saying those are at the center of this federal action against Amazon.
sentences.zh: 而你现在说，这些正是联邦政府针对亚马逊采取行动的核心。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the government is saying there are these very sophisticated mechanisms that let Amazon illegally maintain its monopoly.
sentences.zh: 政府认为，正是这些非常复杂的机制让亚马逊得以非法维持其垄断地位。

sentences.en: That's kind of the core of their argument.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是他们论点的核心。

sentences.en: That behind these things that we all see, there's this grip of power over not just the sellers on Amazon's website, but over the whole Internet.
sentences.zh: 在这些我们所见事物的背后，亚马逊不仅对网站上的卖家，甚至对整个互联网都拥有着强大的控制力。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, I want you to explain this behind the scenes grip on the Internet and consumers and sellers that Amazon has developed through these two items you mentioned.
sentences.zh: 我想请你解释一下，亚马逊通过你提到的这两点，在幕后对互联网、消费者和卖家形成的这种控制力。

sentences.en: And let's start with the buy now button and how, according to our government, that has been misused by Amazon.
sentences.zh: 我们先从“立即购买”按钮说起，根据政府的说法，亚马逊是如何滥用它的。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 没问题。

sentences.en: So, the first thing you have to understand briefly is that most things we buy on Amazon are not actually sold directly by Amazon.
sentences.zh: 首先你需要简要了解的是，我们在亚马逊上买的大多数东西，其实并不是亚马逊直接销售的。

sentences.en: They're sold by outside sellers.
sentences.zh: 它们是由外部卖家销售的。

sentences.en: And these are companies and brands that list their products on Amazon's marketplace.
sentences.zh: 这些公司和品牌将他们的产品列在亚马逊的市场上。

sentences.en: And as a consumer, that whole world of sellers is more or less invisible.
sentences.zh: 作为消费者，整个卖家群体对你来说几乎是隐形的。

sentences.en: Mostly what you see is you go to a product page and you see these big orange and yellow buttons that say, buy now and add to cart.
sentences.zh: 你看到的通常只是产品页面上那些醒目的橙黄色按钮，写着“立即购买”和“加入购物车”。

sentences.en: Or they entice you.
sentences.zh: 或者它们会吸引你。

sentences.en: Free delivery.
sentences.zh: 免费送货。

sentences.en: This could be here tomorrow if you order in the next hour.
sentences.zh: 如果你在接下来的一小时内下单，明天就能送到。

sentences.en: That is called a buy box.
sentences.zh: 这被称为“购买框”。

sentences.en: And so, the government says Amazon has used this buy box, those buttons, as one of its key ways it prevents discounting across the Internet.
sentences.zh: 政府表示，亚马逊利用这个购买框，也就是那些按钮，作为其防止全网降价的关键手段之一。

sentences.en: And how does that work?
sentences.zh: 那它是如何运作的呢？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 是这样的。

sentences.en: So, they're basically saying that Amazon wants to have the lowest price available for a product.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上是说，亚马逊希望某种产品能有最低价。

sentences.en: And it does that, it enforces that by saying, if a product is available on another website, it crawls the web.
sentences.zh: 它通过这种方式强制执行：如果某产品在其他网站上有售，它就会抓取网络信息。

sentences.en: Amazon has these machines that go across, scrapes other websites.
sentences.zh: 亚马逊有专门的机器在网上爬取其他网站的数据。

sentences.en: And if they find it's even one penny less elsewhere, they will essentially punish the seller for that happening.
sentences.zh: 如果他们发现其他地方哪怕便宜了一分钱，他们基本上就会惩罚那个卖家。

sentences.en: And they do that by removing those big, bright buy now and add to cart buttons.
sentences.zh: 他们通过移除那些醒目明亮的“立即购买”和“加入购物车”按钮来做到这一点。

sentences.en: And instead, they make this little button that says, you know, it's just plain black and white text that says, see all buying options.
sentences.zh: 取而代之的是一个不起眼的小按钮，上面只是简单的黑白文字，写着“查看所有购买选项”。

sentences.en: It's like the opposite of calling you to action, the opposite of enticing you to buy.
sentences.zh: 这就像是行动号召的反面，是诱导你购买的反面。

sentences.en: Maybe you've landed on a page like this, I know I have, where it just has, it's like, how do I even buy this thing?
sentences.zh: 也许你遇到过这样的页面，我知道我遇到过，当时我就想，我到底该怎么买这个东西？

sentences.en: It looks like it's unavailable, even though technically it is available.
sentences.zh: 看起来好像没货了，尽管从技术上讲它是有货的。

sentences.en: You're saying that Amazon regularly scours the online retail world and figures out if one of its sellers is simultaneously selling on another online retail platform at a lower price.
sentences.zh: 你是说亚马逊会定期搜寻在线零售世界，看看是否有卖家同时在另一个在线零售平台上以更低的价格销售？

sentences.en: And if it discovers that's the case, it basically demotes that product, and I guess that seller,
sentences.zh: 如果发现这种情况，它基本上就会降低该产品，我想还有该卖家的权重，

sentences.en: on Amazon and makes you not really want to buy their stuff because it doesn't even give you the buy now button.
sentences.zh: 在亚马逊上让你不想买他们的东西，因为它甚至不给你提供“立即购买”按钮。

sentences.en: Exactly, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，正是这样。

sentences.en: So for most sellers, Amazon is a huge portion of their sales.
sentences.zh: 对于大多数卖家来说，亚马逊占据了他们销售额的很大一部分。

sentences.en: And so if the buy button goes away, their sales plummet.
sentences.zh: 所以如果购买按钮消失了，他们的销量就会暴跌。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And then the sellers have to figure out what to do.
sentences.zh: 然后卖家就得想办法解决。

sentences.en: And they can do two things.
sentences.zh: 他们可以做两件事。

sentences.en: They can either raise their price on another website or lower their price on Amazon.
sentences.zh: 要么提高在其他网站上的价格，要么降低在亚马逊上的价格。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And what the FTC in this complaint against Amazon says is that they say Amazon knows that sellers often raise their price elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 联邦贸易委员会在针对亚马逊的诉状中表示，亚马逊知道卖家经常在其他地方提价。

sentences.en: And here's an example of how that might work.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个例子说明它是如何运作的。

sentences.en: So for a story a couple years ago, I spoke with a company called VitaCup, and they make those little coffee pods.
sentences.zh: 几年前为了写一篇报道，我采访了一家叫VitaCup的公司，他们生产那种小咖啡胶囊。

sentences.en: Theirs have vitamins infused in them.
sentences.zh: 他们的胶囊里注入了维生素。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And so they wanted to reach new customers and decided to offer a deal on a different website that has a different model.
sentences.zh: 他们想接触新客户，于是决定在另一个模式不同的网站上提供优惠。

sentences.en: They basically do these flash sales, so deep discounts, but with slow shipping.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上是做这种限时抢购，折扣力度很大，但配送速度较慢。

sentences.en: And so they offer their coffee pods at 30% off on this other website.
sentences.zh: 所以他们在那个网站上将咖啡胶囊打七折出售。

sentences.en: But when Amazon's web crawlers find this, they remove that buy now button.
sentences.zh: 但当亚马逊的网络爬虫发现这一点时，他们就移除了那个“立即购买”按钮。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden, sales plunge.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，销量就暴跌了。

sentences.en: And for VitaCup, like many sellers, like most sellers I've spoken with, Amazon is most of their sales.
sentences.zh: 对于VitaCup来说，就像许多卖家一样，像我采访过的大多数卖家一样，亚马逊占据了他们大部分的销售额。

sentences.en: And so all of a sudden, their biggest outlet, the sales go close to zero for them.
sentences.zh: 所以突然之间，他们最大的销售渠道，销量几乎归零了。

sentences.en: And so they then scramble and they email the other website and said, please take the listing down immediately because I can't afford to lose my Amazon sales like I am.
sentences.zh: 于是他们手忙脚乱地给那个网站发邮件，说请立刻下架商品，因为我承担不起失去亚马逊销量的后果。

sentences.en: So in this example with VitaCup,
sentences.zh: 所以在VitaCup这个例子中，

sentences.en: we clearly see that Amazon's decision to remove the buy now button is so meaningful that the seller takes their product off of a rival website once they lose that button.
sentences.zh: 我们清楚地看到，亚马逊移除“立即购买”按钮的决定影响如此之大，以至于卖家一旦失去该按钮，就会把产品从竞争对手网站上撤下。

sentences.en: It doesn't just raise the price, says, oh, I can't even do business with you anymore, which suggests just how powerful this tactic of removing the buy button really is.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是提价，而是说，噢，我甚至不能再和你做生意了，这说明移除购买按钮这种策略的威力有多大。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, I've talked to sellers who don't even list on other websites at all because they're like, you know, it's not worth losing my sales on Amazon.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我采访过一些卖家，他们根本不在其他网站上架产品，因为他们觉得，为了这点销量失去亚马逊的销售额不值得。

sentences.en: And so the complaint against Amazon is saying this has an effect across the Internet of preventing discounting, that yes, Amazon may have the lowest price,
sentences.zh: 所以针对亚马逊的诉状称，这在整个互联网上产生了阻止降价的效果，是的，亚马逊可能确实有最低价，

sentences.en: but it's actually raising the costs across websites because Amazon is essentially policing what people sell elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 但它实际上抬高了各个网站的成本，因为亚马逊本质上是在监管人们在其他地方卖什么。

sentences.en: Amazon is basically preventing deals from happening elsewhere, which effectively means it has almost sole control over the price in the entire market.
sentences.zh: 亚马逊基本上是在阻止其他地方出现优惠，这意味着它实际上对整个市场的价格拥有几乎唯一的控制权。

sentences.en: That's what the FTC is alleging.
sentences.zh: 这就是联邦贸易委员会所指控的。

sentences.en: And if you know anything about antitrust law, what we are describing here, Karen, sounds a lot like something that is anti-competition and anti-consumer choice.
sentences.zh: 如果你了解反垄断法，凯伦，我们在这里描述的情况听起来非常像那种反竞争和反消费者选择的行为。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because they're saying that this mechanism, this anti-discounting control that Amazon has, that's how they talk about it,
sentences.zh: 因为他们说这种机制，即亚马逊所拥有的这种反降价控制权，他们就是这么说的，

sentences.en: that it has the effect of making it so competitors can't compete on price.
sentences.zh: 其效果就是让竞争对手无法在价格上进行竞争。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: Okay, I think that brings us to the second example that you mentioned, Amazon Prime, perhaps even better known than the buy now button.
sentences.zh: 好的，我想这引出了你提到的第二个例子，亚马逊Prime，可能比“立即购买”按钮更出名。

sentences.en: Everyone enrolls in it, seemingly, because you get really good deals and you get them delivered in insanely fast ways.
sentences.zh: 每个人似乎都加入了，因为你能得到非常好的优惠，而且配送速度快得惊人。

sentences.en: How does the government say that Prime is being abused here?
sentences.zh: 政府认为Prime在这里是如何被滥用的？

sentences.en: They're really focusing on the shipping component of Prime, that Prime is this membership program that, you know, an estimated 170 million American people have.
sentences.zh: 他们真正关注的是Prime的配送部分，Prime是一个会员计划，据估计有1.7亿美国人拥有它。

sentences.en: So this is, you know, most adults in America.
sentences.zh: 所以这基本上是美国的大多数成年人。

sentences.en: Yeah, kind of like half the country.
sentences.zh: 是的，差不多是半个国家。

sentences.en: Half the country if you include kids.
sentences.zh: 如果算上孩子的话就是半个国家。

sentences.en: So like lots of people.
sentences.zh: 所以有很多人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And Prime works because people love Prime, right?
sentences.zh: Prime之所以有效是因为人们喜欢Prime，对吧？

sentences.en: And there's this idea at Amazon, people love great selection, great prices, and fast delivery.
sentences.zh: 亚马逊有一种理念，人们喜欢丰富的选择、优惠的价格和快速的配送。

sentences.en: They will always love those things and you focus on that and you have this flywheel, this virtual circle that consumers love.
sentences.zh: 他们永远会喜欢这些，你专注于此，就会形成这种飞轮效应，这种消费者喜爱的良性循环。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so what's the problem?
sentences.zh: 那问题出在哪里呢？

sentences.en: So the way Amazon has done this is by building all of their logistics infrastructure, warehouses, delivery vans, those vans you see driving down your street all the time.
sentences.zh: 亚马逊的做法是建立他们所有的物流基础设施，仓库、配送货车，就是那些你经常看到在街上行驶的货车。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the FTC is saying that they basically force sellers to use their logistics operation.
sentences.zh: 联邦贸易委员会表示，他们基本上强迫卖家使用他们的物流业务。

sentences.en: How so?
sentences.zh: 怎么说？

sentences.en: Basically to get that checkmark, to get it to say that this is a Prime product, the sellers have had to pay Amazon to use this program called Fulfillment by Amazon.
sentences.zh: 基本上为了获得那个勾选标记，为了显示这是Prime产品，卖家必须付费给亚马逊使用名为“亚马逊物流”的项目。

sentences.en: They have to use Amazon's warehouses.
sentences.zh: 他们必须使用亚马逊的仓库。

sentences.en: They have to use Amazon's logistics, this vast system you just described.
sentences.zh: 他们必须使用亚马逊的物流，也就是你刚才描述的那个庞大系统。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So they send their product to Amazon.
sentences.zh: 所以他们把产品发给亚马逊。

sentences.en: Amazon puts it through all these buildings.
sentences.zh: 亚马逊把产品送进这些建筑里。

sentences.en: When you click buy, pretty much immediately it gets put in a box and put on a truck and to your house.
sentences.zh: 当你点击购买时，几乎立刻它就会被装进盒子里，装上卡车，送到你家。

sentences.en: And it's doing that faster and faster every single day.
sentences.zh: 而且它每天都在变得越来越快。

sentences.en: But if you don't use Amazon's logistics and you don't use their warehouses, then you don't get that checkmark.
sentences.zh: 但如果你不使用亚马逊的物流，不使用他们的仓库，你就得不到那个勾选标记。

sentences.en: You're not Prime eligible.
sentences.zh: 你就没有Prime资格。

sentences.en: And then your sales are going to tank because customers are looking for that.
sentences.zh: 然后你的销量就会暴跌，因为消费者都在寻找那个标记。

sentences.en: We've seen that time and again.
sentences.zh: 我们一次又一次地看到这种情况。

sentences.en: And so sellers know that.
sentences.zh: 卖家也知道这一点。

sentences.en: And it's very hard to build a business on Amazon if you don't ship through Amazon.
sentences.zh: 如果你不通过亚马逊发货，很难在亚马逊上建立业务。

sentences.en: So if you're a seller, this isn't really feeling like that much of a choice.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你是卖家，这感觉并不像是一个真正的选择。

sentences.en: You're basically being compelled to use Amazon's vast logistics system.
sentences.zh: 你基本上是被迫使用亚马逊庞大的物流系统。

sentences.en: Or you're going to be locked out of half of America's buying habits, which are Amazon Prime.
sentences.zh: 否则你就会被排除在美国一半的购买习惯之外，也就是亚马逊Prime。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And when I talk to sellers, they say the more you get into Amazon's logistics, the more you're into the whole Amazon system, the harder it is, the more complicated,
sentences.zh: 当我与卖家交谈时，他们说你越深入亚马逊的物流，你就越深入整个亚马逊系统，就越困难，越复杂，

sentences.en: the more expensive it can be to sell elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 在其他地方销售的成本可能就越高。

sentences.en: Because, you know,
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道，

sentences.en: so much of your sales are on Amazon that you then all of a sudden have to set up a whole different supply chain and figure out different warehouses just gets much more complicated.
sentences.zh: 你的大部分销售额都在亚马逊上，所以你突然之间必须建立一套完全不同的供应链，还要寻找不同的仓库，这变得复杂多了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I'm going to guess that some sellers basically decide, ugh, this is too much of a headache.
sentences.zh: 我猜有些卖家基本上会想，唉，这太让人头疼了。

sentences.en: I'm only going to sell to Amazon, which then calls back to our earlier conversation about the buy button.
sentences.zh: 我只卖给亚马逊，这又回到了我们之前关于购买按钮的对话。

sentences.en: So what you're describing collectively is just a tremendous amount of control.
sentences.zh: 所以你所描述的总体上就是一种巨大的控制力。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Amazon has so much scale, so many orders it's delivering.
sentences.zh: 亚马逊拥有如此大的规模，配送着如此多的订单。

sentences.en: It can deliver them really efficiently, really, really quickly.
sentences.zh: 它能非常高效、非常非常快地完成配送。

sentences.en: And that's incredibly hard to compete with now.
sentences.zh: 现在要与此竞争极其困难。

sentences.en: If you look at the number of warehouses, the number of drivers, the speed of their delivery, it's unsurpassed.
sentences.zh: 如果你看看仓库的数量、司机的数量、配送的速度，它是无与伦比的。

sentences.en: I mean, it is incredible.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这真是不可思议。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so what we as consumers have come to understand as Amazon's brilliance, its ability to be so fast and so cheap, this is why we all use it.
sentences.zh: 所以我们作为消费者所理解的亚马逊的卓越之处，它如此快速和廉价的能力，这就是我们都使用它的原因。

sentences.en: What the FTC is saying is it's actually built on a couple of tactics that ultimately are kind of coercion for sellers.
sentences.zh: 联邦贸易委员会所说的是，它实际上建立在几种策略之上，这些策略最终对卖家来说是一种胁迫。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And that there's a broader effect on consumers,
sentences.zh: 而且这对消费者有更广泛的影响，

sentences.en: that it has an effect of both raising prices and an effect of limiting our choice because there aren't that many places that can viably compete with Amazon anymore.
sentences.zh: 它既有抬高价格的效果，也有限制我们选择的效果，因为现在已经没有多少地方能与亚马逊进行有效竞争了。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 430 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点30分给总统打了电话，他接听了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 太空中的七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60款超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟里最强的队伍。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用不同的起始词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢一锅出的食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》，庆祝成立175周年，致力于帮助您了解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 现在订阅可享受特别优惠，网址是 nytimes.com/subscribe。

sentences.en: Karen, I imagine that Amazon and their lawyers have a very robust defense to this lawsuit.
sentences.zh: 凯伦，我想亚马逊及其律师团队对这起诉讼应该有非常强有力的辩护。

sentences.en: And I wonder if you can represent their counter argument both to the charges about these two specific tactics and to the larger allegation being made by the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你是否能代表他们，针对这两项具体策略的指控，以及美国政府提出的更广泛的指控——即亚马逊具有垄断性、反竞争性且对经济有害——进行反驳。

sentences.en: government that Amazon is being monopolistic, anti-competitive, and bad for the economy.
sentences.zh: 政府认为亚马逊具有垄断性、反竞争性，且对经济有害。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: So when you talk about that buy now button, the buy box, Amazon says, why in the world should we show our customers bad deals?
sentences.zh: 当你谈到那个“立即购买”按钮，即“购买框”时，亚马逊会说，我们为什么要向客户展示糟糕的交易呢？

sentences.en: Why should we knowingly let our customers buy something that we think is not the best deal around?
sentences.zh: 我们为什么要明知故犯，让客户买到我们认为并非最优选的东西？

sentences.en: And people trust us because they know that we can give them the best deal around.
sentences.zh: 人们信任我们，因为他们知道我们能提供最好的交易。

sentences.en: So in some sense, it's kind of a simple argument.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种意义上说，这算是一个简单的论点。

sentences.en: We serve customers and we're not going to do wrong by them.
sentences.zh: 我们服务客户，绝不会亏待他们。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And for Prime and Logistics, they say, look, we've made billions of dollars of investments in these warehouses and let sellers use it.
sentences.zh: 至于Prime会员和物流，他们说，看，我们在这些仓库里投入了数十亿美元，并让卖家使用它们。

sentences.en: That this has actually made it very easy for sellers to build businesses.
sentences.zh: 这实际上让卖家建立业务变得非常容易。

sentences.en: You can build a business without being a supply chain person.
sentences.zh: 你不需要成为供应链专家也能建立业务。

sentences.en: You can just be great at coming up with like this really cool new toy for kids or whatever it is.
sentences.zh: 你只需要擅长构思出像这种非常酷的儿童新玩具之类的东西就行。

sentences.en: They say that it's very well priced, which most sellers I talk to say is true.
sentences.zh: 他们说定价非常合理，我交谈过的大多数卖家也都认同这一点。

sentences.en: And they say it's very easy.
sentences.zh: 而且他们说这非常简单。

sentences.en: And it's actually unlocked this business for so many people and let so many sellers get something that customers love,
sentences.zh: 它实际上为许多人开启了商业机会，让许多卖家能够提供客户喜爱的产品，

sentences.en: which is this unbelievably fast and reliable delivery that we all know and that makes so many things so simple.
sentences.zh: 那就是我们都知道的那种令人难以置信的快速可靠的配送服务，它让许多事情变得如此简单。

sentences.en: And I would say broadly their argument is the FTC has this totally upside down.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，我认为他们的论点是，联邦贸易委员会（FTC）完全搞反了。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: How so?
sentences.zh: 怎么说？

sentences.en: Amazon says that they are the most customer-obsessed company in the world and that every decision they make is what is best for customers.
sentences.zh: 亚马逊声称他们是世界上最以客户为中心的公司，他们所做的每一个决定都是为了客户的最大利益。

sentences.en: We're going to show them the best deal.
sentences.zh: 我们要向他们展示最好的交易。

sentences.en: We're going to get them things fasteSt.
sentences.zh: 我们要以最快的速度把东西送到他们手中。

sentences.en: That they do things with the customer in mind that has had an effect of creating this whole world of sellers that didn't really exiSt.
sentences.zh: 他们所做的一切都是以客户为出发点，这产生了一种效应，创造了一个原本并不存在的卖家世界。

sentences.en: That it's lowered prices broadly over time.
sentences.zh: 这在长期内普遍降低了价格。

sentences.en: That it's just made this whole ecosystem work, essentially, in a way that customers clearly love because they keep coming back for more.
sentences.zh: 这基本上让整个生态系统以一种客户显然喜爱的方式运作，因为他们不断地回来购买。

sentences.en: But in theory and in practice, it's possible for two things to be true at the same time.
sentences.zh: 但在理论和实践中，两件事同时成立是有可能的。

sentences.en: And I'm sure that's what the government is going to say in response to Amazon's response, which is you can be a customer-focused company.
sentences.zh: 我相信这就是政府在回应亚马逊的回应时会说的话，那就是：你可以是一家以客户为中心的公司。

sentences.en: You can be great at delivering fast, discounted products to customers,
sentences.zh: 你可以擅长为客户提供快速、打折的产品，

sentences.en: and you can simultaneously be making life very hard for sellers by eliminating their choices through coercive tactics that ultimately, over time, might be bad for consumers.
sentences.zh: 但同时，你也可以通过强制手段消除卖家的选择，从而让卖家的日子非常难过，而这些手段最终在长期内可能对消费者有害。

sentences.en: I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 我认为你说得对。

sentences.en: There's kind of two sides to this coin.
sentences.zh: 这就像一枚硬币的两面。

sentences.en: It's like, what is good in the Amazon universe for Amazon customers and what is good for customers broadly?
sentences.zh: 就像是，在亚马逊的世界里，什么对亚马逊客户有利，以及什么对广大客户有利？

sentences.en: Are we missing out on things that we don't even know?
sentences.zh: 我们是否错过了我们甚至不知道的东西？

sentences.en: Are we paying more than we even realize we need to be?
sentences.zh: 我们付出的代价是否比我们意识到的还要多？

sentences.en: Are there other websites, other companies that could have started up and done things differently that we don't even—it's like, what don't we know?
sentences.zh: 是否还有其他网站、其他公司本可以起步并以不同的方式做事，而我们甚至不知道——就像是，我们不知道什么？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: What don't we know?
sentences.zh: 我们不知道什么？

sentences.en: Because we so thoroughly live in Amazon's world.
sentences.zh: 因为我们太彻底地生活在亚马逊的世界里了。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So that, of course, raises the question of what will happen to Amazon if it loses this case, and what does the government really want here in the end?
sentences.zh: 所以，这当然引出了一个问题：如果亚马逊输了这场官司会怎样？政府最终到底想要什么？

sentences.en: Does it want to basically turn back the clock, turn back the clock to a time where Amazon doesn't so thoroughly dictate the terms of the American retail landscape?
sentences.zh: 它是想从根本上让时光倒流，回到亚马逊还没有如此彻底地左右美国零售业格局的时代吗？

sentences.en: And if that is the goal, what might that look like?
sentences.zh: 如果那是目标，那会是什么样子？

sentences.en: The government doesn't exactly say what they want.
sentences.zh: 政府并没有明确说明他们想要什么。

sentences.en: They don't say we're going to break Amazon up.
sentences.zh: 他们没有说我们要拆分亚马逊。

sentences.en: They just say we want to undo these things.
sentences.zh: 他们只是说我们想要撤销这些事情。

sentences.en: And what Amazon says is that it's going to force them to unwind all these things that customers love.
sentences.zh: 而亚马逊表示，这将迫使他们撤销所有客户喜爱的服务。

sentences.en: They won't be able to offer their prices.
sentences.zh: 他们将无法提供现在的价格。

sentences.en: They won't be able to make it as easy and as simple as possible.
sentences.zh: 他们将无法做到尽可能简单方便。

sentences.en: These are the things that keep us coming back for more.
sentences.zh: 这些就是让我们不断回购的原因。

sentences.en: All these things, they have to unwind it.
sentences.zh: 所有这些，他们都必须撤销。

sentences.en: And that's very hard to do.
sentences.zh: 这非常难做到。

sentences.en: And I know because I tried to do it myself.
sentences.zh: 我知道，因为我自己尝试过。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你是什么意思？

sentences.en: About a year ago, my husband and I did something that very few people do, which is we canceled our Prime subscription.
sentences.zh: 大约一年前，我和我丈夫做了一件很少有人做的事，那就是我们取消了Prime订阅。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 哈。

sentences.en: You predicted that there was going to be an antitrust case.
sentences.zh: 你预见到会有一场反垄断诉讼。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And you just went ahead and said, what will this future potentially look like?
sentences.zh: 你就直接说，这个未来可能会是什么样子？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, it did come out of reporting, though.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这确实是出于报道工作。

sentences.en: This was not a protest thing.
sentences.zh: 这不是一种抗议行为。

sentences.en: This was not like an Amazon's bad thing.
sentences.zh: 这也不是因为觉得亚马逊不好。

sentences.en: This was us looking at our finances.
sentences.zh: 这是我们审视自己的财务状况。

sentences.en: And we felt like many Americans, we spent a lot of money in the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 我们感觉像许多美国人一样，在疫情期间花了很多钱。

sentences.en: We were just buying a lot of stuff.
sentences.zh: 我们当时只是买了太多东西。

sentences.en: And we wanted to buy less stuff.
sentences.zh: 我们想少买点东西。

sentences.en: And so I know from reporting, we know from what Amazon tells sellers, we know from our own experience that the easier things are to buy, the more you buy them.
sentences.zh: 所以我从报道中知道，从亚马逊告诉卖家的话中知道，从我们自己的经验中知道，购买越容易，你买得就越多。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And nothing's easier than Amazon Prime.
sentences.zh: 没有什么比亚马逊Prime更容易了。

sentences.en: So you drop it.
sentences.zh: 所以你放弃了它。

sentences.en: So we dropped it.
sentences.zh: 所以我们放弃了它。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: It was an experiment.
sentences.zh: 这是一个实验。

sentences.en: Would we miss it?
sentences.zh: 我们会想念它吗？

sentences.en: Would we agree we'd pay for fast shipping when we wanted it?
sentences.zh: 我们会同意在需要时支付快速配送费吗？

sentences.en: We wouldn't when we didn't.
sentences.zh: 不需要时我们就不会付。

sentences.en: We might put things in the cart, but not click buy eventually.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会把东西放进购物车，但最终不点击购买。

sentences.en: And we were just curious, like, what would happen?
sentences.zh: 我们只是好奇，会发生什么？

sentences.en: And so?
sentences.zh: 然后呢？

sentences.en: What happens?
sentences.zh: 发生了什么？

sentences.en: Tell us about this alternate universe.
sentences.zh: 告诉我们这个平行宇宙的情况。

sentences.en: It's very weird.
sentences.zh: 非常奇怪。

sentences.en: It's like you have to plan ahead a little bit.
sentences.zh: 就像你必须提前做一点计划。

sentences.en: I found that I spent more on other websites as a result of it.
sentences.zh: 我发现结果是我在其他网站上花得更多了。

sentences.en: You know, Target.
sentences.zh: 你知道，塔吉特百货（Target）。

sentences.en: There's one year my kid's swim class.
sentences.zh: 有一年我孩子的游泳课。

sentences.en: I put things to buy online and pick up in their store, and I go and swing by and get it.
sentences.zh: 我在线购买并选择到店自取，然后顺路去拿。

sentences.en: I also found that we did buy less.
sentences.zh: 我还发现我们确实买得少了。

sentences.en: You know, there were things that I searched for.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有些东西我搜索过。

sentences.en: And when I saw it wouldn't be available in the time for when I wanted it, we just didn't buy it.
sentences.zh: 当我看到它无法在我想要的时间内送达时，我们就干脆不买了。

sentences.en: You know, I remember we were going camping with friends.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我记得我们和朋友去露营。

sentences.en: And I was considering getting these reusable water balloons, which are a thing with kids these days.
sentences.zh: 我当时在考虑买那些可重复使用的水气球，这在现在的孩子中很流行。

sentences.en: They're kind of cool.
sentences.zh: 它们挺酷的。

sentences.en: They don't produce the scraps all over the ground.
sentences.zh: 它们不会在地上留下碎片。

sentences.en: And I couldn't get it fast enough.
sentences.zh: 但我无法足够快地拿到它。

sentences.en: And so we just didn't buy it before we went camping.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在去露营前就没买。

sentences.en: And guess what?
sentences.zh: 你猜怎么着？

sentences.en: Camping was okay.
sentences.zh: 露营也挺好的。

sentences.en: But then there were other times, like I had the Seattle Bureau for the New York Times over for a barbecue.
sentences.zh: 但后来也有其他时候，比如我邀请《纽约时报》西雅图分社的人来烧烤。

sentences.en: And I wanted to get something for the kids to play with outside.
sentences.zh: 我想给孩子们买点户外玩的东西。

sentences.en: So I ordered these little tiny soccer goals, and we paid $8 or whatever for the shipping.
sentences.zh: 所以我订了这些小小的足球门，我们支付了8美元左右的运费。

sentences.en: And I got there before the weekend.
sentences.zh: 周末前送到了。

sentences.en: And the kids actually spent a ton of time playing with their soccer goals.
sentences.zh: 孩子们确实花了很多时间玩这些足球门。

sentences.en: Broadly, I definitely spent way less on shipping because I realized very few things are quite that urgent.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，我绝对在运费上省了很多钱，因为我意识到很少有东西是那么紧急的。

sentences.en: It's striking to me, Karen, your experience.
sentences.zh: 凯伦，你的经历让我印象深刻。

sentences.en: In some ways, like you said, you are kind of making the case for Amazon because what you have found is that there's life beyond Amazon.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，就像你说的，你其实是在为亚马逊辩护，因为你发现亚马逊之外还有生活。

sentences.en: You can opt out of it, and you're fine.
sentences.zh: 你可以选择退出，而且你过得很好。

sentences.en: Therefore, it's a little hard to think of them as a coercive monopoly that you can't avoid in our economy.
sentences.zh: 因此，很难把他们看作是我们经济中无法避开的强制性垄断者。

sentences.en: But on the other hand, what you're describing, the experience you're having,
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，你所描述的经历，

sentences.en: requires you to have a totally rethought version of being a consumer than the one the rest of us have gotten used to quite happily.
sentences.zh: 要求你拥有一种完全重构的消费者心态，这与我们其他人已经习惯并乐在其中的心态完全不同。

sentences.en: And you have volunteered to have a more burdensome version of buying stuff, waiting for it, diversifying your shopping experience, driving to a store, God forbid.
sentences.zh: 你自愿选择了一种更繁琐的购物方式：等待送货、分散购物渠道、开车去商店——天哪，太麻烦了。

sentences.en: So you're kind of making Amazon's point.
sentences.zh: 所以你既是在支持亚马逊的观点，

sentences.en: You're also kind of undermining it.
sentences.zh: 又在某种程度上削弱了它。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Amazon fundamentally changed what we all expect.
sentences.zh: 亚马逊从根本上改变了我们所有人的期望。

sentences.en: I mean, even in the years since I stopped having Prime, their shipping speeds for Prime have dramatically improved.
sentences.zh: 我是说，即使在我停止使用Prime的这几年里，他们的Prime配送速度也得到了显著提高。

sentences.en: They're faster than they've ever been.
sentences.zh: 他们比以往任何时候都快。

sentences.en: They've built all these warehouses in the pandemic, and now they are putting them to use like you would not believe.
sentences.zh: 他们在疫情期间建造了所有这些仓库，现在他们正在以你无法想象的方式利用它们。

sentences.en: They're getting things so faSt.
sentences.zh: 他们送货太快了。

sentences.en: They have taught us how to shop online, basically.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上教会了我们如何在线购物。

sentences.en: And that is very hard to unwind as a consumer.
sentences.zh: 作为消费者，这非常难改变。

sentences.en: I did it as an experiment, and I'm an outlier, and I don't even know.
sentences.zh: 我把它当作一个实验，我是个特例，我甚至不知道。

sentences.en: Like, we may still rejoin Prime.
sentences.zh: 比如，我们可能还会重新加入Prime。

sentences.en: We haven't even decided because there are definitely times where I'm like, oh, man, this would have been really nice to have.
sentences.zh: 我们还没决定，因为确实有几次我会想，噢，天哪，如果有这个东西该多好。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, ultimately what you're saying is no matter what happens here, no matter how this case gets resolved, it's going to be really hard, perhaps even impossible,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，归根结底，无论这里发生什么，无论这起案件如何解决，要改变我们作为消费者的思维方式，将是非常困难的，甚至是不可能的。

sentences.en: to un-rewire our brains in the way that Amazon has as consumers.
sentences.zh: 要改变我们作为消费者的思维方式。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: They have taught us that we can go to them, open, click, buy, the item shows up at your doorstep that day, done.
sentences.zh: 他们教会了我们，我们可以去找他们，打开页面，点击，购买，商品当天就会出现在你的门口，搞定。

sentences.en: I mean, that's a very hard loop to break.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个非常难打破的循环。

sentences.en: Well, Karen, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好吧，凯伦，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: Anytime.
sentences.zh: 随时欢迎。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wynna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是Wynna Liu。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games, and I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我编写了《纽约时报》游戏中的“Connections”拼图，我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog, and I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗，也喜欢尝试捉弄你。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖尔斯基，我每天负责制作《拼字蜜蜂》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做“联觉”的特质。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由真人制作的，就像你刚才听到的那样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games，今天就开始玩吧。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的内容。

sentences.en: I have very good news for the country.
sentences.zh: 我有一个对全国来说非常好的消息。

sentences.en: Democrats and Republicans have come to an agreement, and the government will remain open.
sentences.zh: 民主党和共和党已经达成协议，政府将继续正常运作。

sentences.en: Over the weekend, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 周末期间，美国

sentences.en: government narrowly averted a shutdown that had appeared to be all but certain after Republican House Speaker Kevin McCarthy put forth a short-term spending bill
sentences.zh: 政府惊险地避免了停摆，而在此前，在共和党众议院议长凯文·麦卡锡提出一项短期支出法案后，停摆似乎已成定局，

sentences.en: that won more support from House Democrats than it did from House Republicans.
sentences.zh: 该法案获得的众议院民主党人支持比共和党人还要多。

sentences.en: Hours later, that bill was adopted by the Democratic-controlled U.S.
sentences.zh: 几小时后，该法案在民主党控制的美国

sentences.en: Senate and signed by President Biden, moments before the government was scheduled to shut down.
sentences.zh: 参议院获得通过，并在政府预定停摆的前一刻由拜登总统签署生效。

sentences.en: The bipartisan outcome was the exact scenario that McCarthy had sought to avoid for fear of upsetting the House's far-right membership, who unanimously voted against the bill,
sentences.zh: 这种两党合作的结果正是麦卡锡一直试图避免的局面，因为他担心会激怒众议院的极右翼成员，他们一致投票反对该法案，

sentences.en: and who may now use it as a pretext to try to remove McCarthy as House Speaker in the coming days.
sentences.zh: 而且他们现在可能会以此为借口，在未来几天试图罢免麦卡锡的众议院议长职务。

sentences.en: During a news conference, McCarthy said he was willing to take that risk.
sentences.zh: 在新闻发布会上，麦卡锡表示他愿意承担这种风险。

sentences.en: If somebody wants to make a motion against me, bring it.
sentences.zh: 如果有人想对我提出动议，尽管放马过来。

sentences.en: There has to be an adult in the room.
sentences.zh: 总得有个成年人来主持大局。

sentences.en: Democrats, especially in the Senate, celebrated the moment as both an economic and political victory, and as a chance to scold House Republicans for their partisanship.
sentences.zh: 民主党人，尤其是参议院的民主党人，将这一时刻视为经济和政治上的双重胜利，并借此机会斥责众议院共和党人的党派偏见。

sentences.en: If there is one lesson for House Republicans to take from the absolute chaos they have caused this past week, it is that partisanship is not a path forward.
sentences.zh: 如果说众议院共和党人能从过去一周他们造成的混乱中吸取什么教训的话，那就是党派偏见绝非前进之路。

sentences.en: It's a path to chaos.
sentences.zh: 那是一条通往混乱的道路。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Rob Zipko, Asta Chaturvedi, Will Reed, and Jessica Chung.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由罗布·齐普科、阿斯塔·查图尔维迪、威尔·里德和杰西卡·钟制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Mark George, Lisa Chow, and Devin Taylor.
sentences.zh: 由马克·乔治、丽莎·周和德文·泰勒编辑。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Lansford of Wonderland.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderland的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰斯福德创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一台严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了一批自称改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场激烈、混乱，有时甚至令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《地铁》节目中，我，莎拉·凯尼格，将讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中逐渐失控的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《地铁》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在你收听播客的任何平台订阅收听。

sentences.en: Let's read your comments.
sentences.zh: 让我们来读读你们的评论。

sentences.en: Let's read.
sentences.zh: 让我们开始读吧。
